main_reasons: Loss per share appears to exclude large deemed dividends from warrant inducements ($7.6M Feb-2025, $4.5M Dec-2025, $5.0M in 2024); EPS of $(3.16)/$(5.84) equals net loss plus only the small preferred dividend divided by weighted shares, so loss attributable to common and EPS look materially understated
Management reports material weaknesses (segregation of duties, missing written policies and control documentation); disclosure controls are not effective; small finance staff

Going concern opinion with recurring losses ($19.4M on $16.1M sales) and dependence on serial dilutive warrant inducements and a Reg A raise; MD&A says cash is sufficient for 12 months while Note 2 and the auditor cite substantial doubt

Many internal inconsistencies and sloppy notes: warrant exercise counts (755,558 vs 1,295,000 vs 1,295,091), Series C share counts (427,812 vs 472,812), financing cash flow total ($19.46M vs $19.50M), wrong dates, blank percentages in the concentration and lease notes
Bitcoin holdings are promoted (doubled holdings, Coinbase custody) but no digital-asset line item, fair-value accounting or disclosure appears in the financial statements
Equity accounting is complex and error-prone (auditor CAM): large share subscriptions payable ($5.4M) for unissued warrant shares, Black-Scholes valuations, and frequent equity-for-services issuances
Inventory is 57% of current assets and rose 84% with soft-cover sales collapsing, and the obsolescence reserve is a judgmental CAM; segment cost allocations shifted sharply between years
Founder CEO controls 51% of the vote through Series A preferred, is paid through his own consulting entity, and his father runs a subsidiary; promotional MD&A; small regional audit firm
Mitigants: revenue growth is backed by low receivables (mostly online and DTC sales), cash flows tie, only one audit adjustment, and there is no restatement, auditor change or litigation
